title: Minimum and Maximum in One Pass
statement:
Returning two values from a C++ function is most naturally done with a
`std::pair` (or a small struct) -- no output parameters needed.

## Your function

```
std::pair<int, int> MinMax(const std::vector<int>& values);
```

`values` is **never empty**. Return `{smallest, largest}`.

## Watch out

- **Do not seed the minimum with `0` or the maximum with `0`.** An
  all-positive array has a minimum above zero and an all-negative one has
  a maximum below zero; starting from `0` reports a value that is not in
  the array at all.
- **Seed both from `values[0]`** and compare from the second element on --
  that is correct for every non-empty array, including one made of
  `INT_MIN` or `INT_MAX`.

tests.name: a single element is both minimum and maximum
all positive -- the minimum is not 0
tests.description: Seeding the minimum with 0 would report 0.

tests.name: all negative -- the maximum is not 0
tests.description: Seeding the maximum with 0 would report 0.
